newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Selective buying lifts Singapore shares at close.
newsitem.headline: Selective buying lifts Singapore shares at close.

text.p: The Singapore stocks were mostly firmer on Wednesday amid selective buying of property and banking stocks, dealers said.
"People are lifting their weightings and increasing their current positions slightly because these companies saw better than expected 1996 earnings," said a dealer.
Buys included property counters like City Developments, Keppel Land and DBS Land, banking stocks like OCBC, OUB and DBS as well as blue-chip Singapore Press Holding (SPH).
However, there was no rush to buy as caution still prevailed on fears of more downside on Wall Street, dealers said.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index ended up 15.14 points at 2,089.81. Turnover was a moderate 147.9 million shares, with losers outpacing gainers by 232 to 144.
The foreign tranche of SPH and CityDev led gainers, rising S$0.80 and S$0.60 respectively to end at S$27.70 and S$13.40.
Debutante Excel Machine led the actives with more than 11 million shares traded. The stock ended at S$0.645 against its initial public offer of S$0.63.
